title: P0: Unauthenticated public GRASP Git Smart HTTP (no Gitea auth leak)
description: internal/api/githttp_npub.go reverse-proxies to Gitea which enforces Basic auth before the pre-receive hook runs. Keep public Smart HTTP unauthenticated; authenticate bridge-to-Gitea internally with a scoped service identity; strip caller Authorization/proxy-auth/cookies; never surface WWW-Authenticate: Basic; inject backend authority only after npub/identifier mapping succeeds; fail closed if the pre-receive hook is missing. Acceptance: git ls-remote without credentials works; mismatching push rejected by hook not 401. [Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]
close_reason: Proxy hardening implemented + tested. Deployment still needs a scoped Gitea service account exposed as GIT_BACKEND_USER/GIT_BACKEND_PASSWORD and private-network restriction of the backend — covered by final gate phase1-boi.

title: GRASP-01 compliance for grasp.sharegap.net (sharegap issue #2)

Core rule: Git Smart HTTP is unauthenticated; push authorization comes from signed Nostr repository-state events, not Gitea credentials. Definition of done: canonical single host, credential-free clone/push, signed-state authorization, grasp-audit passes, real ngit flow succeeds.

title: P1: Durable purgatory for events awaiting git data
description: Retain accepted 30617/30618/PR/PR-update events but do not serve until related Git data arrives; discard after 30 minutes. Durable storage (not memory), purgatory ack on acceptance, excluded from normal queries, atomic release, NIP-01 replaceable ordering preserved, restart-safe. [Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]

title: P1: Harden signed-state selection (NIP-01 ordering + recursive maintainers)

[Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]

title: P1: Handle ref deletion in pre-receive and reconciliation
description: Pre-receive compares newSHA to state entries; git signals deletion with all-zero object id while state omits deleted refs. Treat zero newSHA as deletion; accept when latest authorized state omits the ref; reject while state declares it; reconcile local refs by deleting refs omitted from authoritative state; test atomic mixed pushes. [Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]
close_reason: Deletion semantics in pre-receive + omitted-ref pruning in proactivesync, with mixed-push and namespace-safety tests.

title: Audit internal/signer ConnectBunker context lifetime (NIP-46 response subscription)
description: netward's fix 854c559 (tag archive/sharegap/netward-fp-32) found that passing a short-lived handshake context to nip46.ConnectBunker silently cancels the long-lived response subscription, so startup succeeds but later signing calls hang. Verify main's internal/signer/service.go connectNIP46Bunker/signerForGrant paths don't pass request-scoped contexts to ConnectBunker; apply an equivalent fix if they do.
close_reason: Confirmed the bug on both CreateGrant and signerForGrant paths; fixed with cancellation-detached connect bounded by 30s handshake timeout; regression test added.

title: Migrate grasp-gitea from nbd-wtf/go-nostr to fiatjaf.com/nostr
description: The nbd-wtf/go-nostr package is deprecated. Replace all usages with fiatjaf.com/nostr (already a dependency in go.mod). This is a deep API migration: keys/IDs/sigs/kinds move from hex strings to typed [32]byte/[64]byte/uint16; GetPublicKey no longer returns error; RelayConnect requires RelayOptions; event.Sign takes [32]byte; Filter fields are typed; nip19/nip34/nip46/nip05 signatures changed. Drop the old dependency via go mod tidy when complete.
design:
API mapping nbd-wtf/go-nostr v0.52 -> fiatjaf.com/nostr:
TYPES (hex string -> typed): Event.ID string->nostr.ID[32]byte; Event.PubKey string->nostr.PubKey[32]byte; Event.Sig string->[64]byte; Event.Kind int->nostr.Kind(uint16). Convert at store/Gitea/log boundaries via .Hex() and PubKeyFromHex/IDFromHex.
KEYS: GeneratePrivateKey()string -> Generate()SecretKey; GetPublicKey(hex)(string,err) -> GetPublicKey([32]byte)PubKey (no err); IsValidPublicKey(hex) -> use PubKeyFromHex err; nip19.Decode nsec returns [32]byte not string; nip19 Encode* take typed args.
SIGN/VERIFY: event.Sign(hexkey) -> Sign([32]byte); event.CheckSignature()(bool,err) -> VerifySignature()bool; CheckID()bool unchanged.
FILTER: Kinds []int->[]Kind; Authors []string->[]PubKey; IDs []string->[]ID.
RELAY (redesigned): RelayConnect(ctx,url) -> RelayConnect(ctx,url,RelayOptions{}); QuerySync REMOVED -> use QueryEvents(filter) iter.Seq[Event] or pool; Subscribe(ctx,[]Filter) -> Subscribe(ctx,Filter,SubscriptionOptions{}); sub.Events chan; EndOfStoredEvents handling changed; Publish(ctx,Event) value.
NIP34: repo.Maintainers []string -> []nostr.PubKey; Parse* take nostr.Event value.
NIP46: signatures typed. Existing server_signer.go already bridges both pkgs via JSON.
PLAN: (1) flip internal event type wholesale; (2) fix boundary conversions at store layer; (3) rework relay subscribe/query call sites; (4) migrate 25 src files then 21 tests; (5) go build+test green; (6) go mod tidy to drop nbd-wtf.
notes: COMPLETE (on branch migrate-fiatjaf-nostr). All grasp-gitea code + tests migrated nbd-wtf/go-nostr -> fiatjaf.com/nostr. Also migrated khatru+eventstore (used by embedded relay + integration test relay) to fiatjaf.com/nostr/khatru + fiatjaf.com/nostr/eventstore because khatru's API redesigned (single-func handlers, UseEventstore, iterator queries). nbd-wtf fully removed from go.mod/go.sum via go mod tidy. Verified: go build/vet/test ./... AND -tags full all pass (exit 0). Key boundary decision: used PubKeyFromHexCheap (decode-only) for stored-pubkey conversions in webhook to preserve original non-curve-validating behavior. NOT yet committed/pushed.
close_reason: Migrated grasp-gitea from nbd-wtf/go-nostr to fiatjaf.com/nostr; nbd-wtf removed from go.mod/go.sum; default + -tags full build/vet/test all pass

title: GRASP-02: periodic (<=1h) proactive git-data sync from clone servers + historic/live event sync from announcement relays
description: Audit docs/reviews/grasp-compliance-audit.md GRASP-02. proactivesync only updates refs for objects ALREADY present locally (updateRefIfObjectExists); there is no periodic timer and no git fetch from the announcement's clone URLs, and the subscriber does live sync from CONFIGURED relays only (no per-announcement relays-tag sync, no historic backfill). GRASP-02 MUST: (1) proactively sync matching Nostr events (historic + live) from each accepted announcement's relays tag; (2) sync missing git data from the clone servers no less than every 1h. Add a scheduler + git fetch from clone URLs into the mirrored repo.
close_reason: proactivesync now runs a ticker (default 1h, clamped <=1h via NormalizeSyncInterval): each tick lists mappings, validates the cached owner-signed announcement, backfills historic state/PR events from the announcement relays (paged Until), git-fetches missing state objects from the clone URLs, and reconciles refs. Injectable ticker/gitRunner/relay for deterministic tests. Wired in main.go.

title: GRASP-01 #5: git-HTTP must be reachable at /<npub>/<identifier>.git (architectural)
description: Audit docs/reviews/grasp-compliance-audit.md item G01-5. Stock Gitea serves /<orgname>/<repo>.git and the bridge provisions repos under a NIP-05-resolved org name, not an npub. GRASP-01 MUST serve git smart-HTTP at /<npub>/<percent-encoded-identifier>.git. Reconcile via ONE of: (a) an /<npub>/... route or reverse-proxy/redirect (nginx or Gitea fork) mapping npub->org, or (b) provision the Gitea owner AS the npub, or (c) document an explicit, accepted divergence. Product+architecture decision required.
close_reason: Bridge-side git smart-HTTP reverse proxy (internal/api/githttp_npub.go): matches /<npub>/<percent-encoded-id>.git/{info/refs,git-upload-pack,git-receive-pack}, looks up (npub,repo-id) in the store -> Gitea owner/repo, and streams via httputil.ReverseProxy to GITEA_URL rewritten to /<org>/<repo>.git/...; 404 on unknown, OPTIONS 204, fixed GRASP-01 CORS. EscapedPath preserves encoded slashes; identifier percent-decoded. Deploy note added: route public npub .git paths to the bridge. Tested.

title: GRASP-01 #3: embedded relay must accept collaboration events (1617/1618/1619/1621/1630-1633/1111) referencing accepted repos
description: Audit docs/reviews/grasp-compliance-audit.md item G01-3. cmd/grasp-bridge/embedded_full.go RejectEvent rejects everything except kinds 30617/30618. GRASP-01 MUST also accept events that tag, or are tagged by, accepted announcements/issues/patches — i.e. patches (1617), PRs (1618/1619), issues (1621), status (1630-1633), NIP-22 comments (1111). Implement an accept policy that admits these kinds when they reference (via 'a'/'e') an accepted 30617 (or an accepted issue/patch), and still rejects unrelated spam. Converges with the user-signed migration Phase F (bidirectional ingest).
close_reason: Embedded relay now accepts collaboration events (1617/1618/1619/1621/1630-1633/1111) referencing a hosted repo (a=30617:pk:id via mapping store) or stored issue/patch/PR (e/E); rejects unrelated. Tested. cmd/grasp-bridge/embedded_full.go

title: Phase B: Outbound signing queue (persistent, idempotent, retry/backoff/dead-letter)
description: Plan section 9-B / 4 in docs/designs/user-signed-nip34-migration.md. Add outbound_events table (id, dedupe_key UNIQUE, kind, author_pubkey, scope, unsigned_json, state, attempts, next_attempt_at, last_error, created_at, published_event_id) and a worker that drains it: build unsigned event -> SignWithGrant(author) -> publishToRelays -> mark done; on signer-offline/error, backoff + retry, and dead-letter past a TTL. At-least-once with idempotent publish (dedupe_key). Metrics for depth/age/failures + an admin endpoint to inspect the queue.
acceptance_criteria: events enqueue and publish exactly once on success; offline signer causes bounded retry then dead-letter; metrics + admin visibility; tests cover success, retry, and dead-letter paths
close_reason: Phase B done: internal/outbox persistent signing queue (outbound_events table, dedupe_key idempotency, exp-backoff retry, max-attempts+TTL dead-letter), publisher.PublishSigned, metrics + admin /outbound-events endpoint, wired in main.go. 6 deterministic tests. Gate green incl -tags full.

title: Phase C: Route owner-authored events (30618 state) through user signing
description: Plan section 9-C / 5 in docs/designs/user-signed-nip34-migration.md. Establish the owner signer grant at provisioning (bind to owner pubkey). Route kind:30618 repo state through the Phase B queue signed by the OWNER grant instead of BRIDGE_NSEC. Keep 5401 CI operator-signed (attestation). Remove bridge-signing of owner content from publisher.buildStateEvent path. 30617 announcement already owner-signed (unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: 30618 state events are signed by the owner pubkey (verified) and published via the queue; no owner-content path signs with BRIDGE_NSEC; 5401 unchanged; integration test with mock bunker
close_reason: Phase C done: 30618 repo state now built unsigned/owner-authored and enqueued to the outbox for owner-grant signing (dedupe repo-state:<id>:<digest>); bridge-signed fallback + metric when signer disabled/no grant. POST /signer/authorize creates owner grants. 5401/30617 unchanged. Tests + gate green incl -tags full.

title: Phase A: Persistent NIP-46 signer foundation (durable grants + BunkerClient pool)
description: Plan section 9-A / 4 / 7 in docs/designs/user-signed-nip34-migration.md. Wire a real BunkerConnector using github.com/nbd-wtf/go-nostr/nip46 (ConnectBunker + BunkerClient.SignEvent/Ping/GetPublicKey) — currently main.go:102 passes nil. Add signer_grants table (pubkey PK, client_seckey_enc, bunker_uri_enc, relays, permissions, granted_at, revoked_at, last_ok_at, status) with at-rest encryption (NaCl secretbox/age, master key from env). Build a Signer Service with an in-memory BunkerClient pool keyed by pubkey (lazy reconnect from stored grant, Ping health, GetPublicKey identity check). Expose SignWithGrant(ctx, pubkey, *nostr.Event). Tests against a mock/in-process bunker.
acceptance_criteria: signer_grants table + encryption; SignWithGrant signs via a live BunkerClient and verifies the resulting signature; grant creation rejected if bunker GetPublicKey != claimed pubkey; unit tests with mock bunker pass
close_reason: Phase A done: internal/signer with encrypted signer_grants storage (nacl/secretbox, SIGNER_MASTER_KEY), CreateGrant (ConnectBunker+GetPublicKey verify), BunkerClient pool (lazy reconnect+Ping), SignWithGrant, BunkerSigner interface for tests. Wired (constructed) in main.go. Gate green incl -tags full.

title: EPIC: Fully user-signed events (NIP-46) + full NIP-34 compliance
description: Migrate from gateway-signed to fully user-signed NIP-34 events via NIP-46 remote signers, with signing authorization bound to the repo owner pubkey at provisioning, and expand to full NIP-34 compliance (patch-based PRs, NIP-22 comments, euc, maintainers, bidirectional Nostr<->Gitea sync). Full plan: docs/designs/user-signed-nip34-migration.md. Current NIP-46 is auth-only (connector nil in main.go:102, no persistent grant); this epic builds durable remote signing + an outbound signing queue. Children are phased A-G.
close_reason: EPIC complete: user-signed NIP-46 migration + full NIP-34 compliance shipped. A signer foundation (encrypted grants + BunkerClient pool), B outbound signing queue, C owner-signed 30618, D contributor-signed collaboration events (queue-until-linked), E NIP-34 tag-schema compliance + NIP-22 1111 + euc, F Nostr->Gitea reflection w/ echo-loop prevention, G docs; plus 10317 owner cache/rebroadcast. Transition fallbacks keep legacy bridge-signed mode when SIGNER_MASTER_KEY unset. Documented deferrals: full patch-apply, pre-link backfill.

title: internal/webhook has zero test coverage
description: internal/webhook (handler.go 403 LOC, types.go 141 LOC) is a live HTTP handler wired at /webhook/gitea in cmd/grasp-bridge/main.go, yet has NO test files (go test reports 'no test files'). It handles HMAC verification, JSON payload parsing for 6 event types (push/create/delete/pull_request/issues/label), and maps them to signed NIP-34 Nostr events. Zero tests means the npub/hex tag bug (see sibling issue) shipped undetected, and any regression in payload parsing or event mapping is invisible. Scope: add handler_test.go covering (1) HMAC accept/reject, (2) method-not-allowed, (3) push -> RepublishForGiteaRepo delegation + CI push hook, (4) pull_request opened/closed -> correct kinds & hex tags, (5) issues opened/closed & labeled -> kinds 1621/1985 with valid hex 'p' and '30617:hex:repo' 'a' tags, (6) unknown-repo webhook is a silent no-op. Use a fake publisher/relay to assert the exact events produced.
acceptance_criteria: webhook package has tests; go test ./internal/webhook passes; tests assert hex pubkeys and valid a-tag coordinates in emitted events
close_reason: Added internal/webhook/handler_test.go: 8 tests covering HMAC accept/reject, method-not-allowed, push delegation+CI hook, unknown-repo no-op, PR opened/merged, issue opened/labeled, and hex-tag regression guards. Introduced Publisher interface for testability.

title: Webhook NIP-34 events use bech32 npub instead of hex pubkey in p/a tags
description: internal/webhook/handler.go builds NIP-34 events (kind 1618/1619/1621/1630-1633/1985) using mapping.Npub (bech32) for 'p' tags and for the repo 'a'-tag coordinate (repoTag = npub/RepoID). Nostr 'p' tags MUST be 32-byte hex pubkeys, and NIP-34 addressable coordinates must be '30617:<hex-pubkey>:<repo-id>'. Consequences: (1) every PR/issue/label/status event is non-compliant and invisible to clients filtering #p by hex; (2) the 'a' coordinate 'npub.../repo' is entirely malformed and cannot be resolved to the repo announcement. The publisher (buildStateEvent, buildWorkflowRunEvent in ci.go) correctly uses mapping.Pubkey (hex), proving the intended pattern. Fix: use mapping.Pubkey for all p tags and build a-tags as fmt.Sprintf('%d:%s:%s', 30617, mapping.Pubkey, mapping.RepoID). Evidence: handler.go lines ~186-300 (repoTag, prRef, {p, mapping.Npub}).
close_reason: Fixed: webhook handler now uses mapping.Pubkey (hex) for all 'p' tags and builds 'a' coordinates as 30617:<hex>:<repo-id> via new repoAddr() helper. Covered by new regression tests (TestNoNpubInSemanticTags, TestPR/Issue_*).

title: Pre-link backfill: publish contributor events created before they linked a NIP-46 signer
description: Phase D decision #1 skips collaboration events from unlinked actors (unlinked_actor_skipped metric) and never publishes them. Implement backfill: when the webhook skips an unlinked actor, PERSIST the fully-built unsigned event template in a new pending_actor_events table keyed by the Gitea sender user id (kind, unsigned_event_json, scope, dedupe_key, created_at). When that Gitea user later links a signer via NIP-46 login (auth CreateGrant + identity link resolves gitea_user_id <-> pubkey), trigger a backfill: load pending rows for that user id, set each event's PubKey to the now-known pubkey, Enqueue into the outbox (author=pubkey, same dedupe_key), and clear the rows. Reuses the Phase B outbox + Phase A grant. Bound the backlog (cap rows/age) so it can't grow unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: an unlinked contributor's PR/issue event is persisted instead of dropped; after that user links a signer, the pending events are enqueued to the outbox under their pubkey and the rows cleared; dedupe_key prevents double-publish; backlog is capped; tests cover persist-on-skip and enqueue-on-link
close_reason: Pre-link backfill: unlinked-actor events persisted to pending_actor_events (keyed by gitea_user_id, capped 500/user + 30d, dedupe idempotent) instead of dropped; NIP-46 login triggers ActorBackfiller.EnqueuePending which sets PubKey=linked pubkey and enqueues each pending event to the outbox then deletes the row. title: Harden reflector echo-loop guard against dropped/duplicate Gitea webhooks
description: The echo guard (reflected_events.echo_pending one-shot, ConsumeReflectedGiteaEcho) is fragile: (1) DROPPED webhook — if the Gitea webhook resulting from a reflection never fires, echo_pending stays 1 forever, so a genuine LATER Gitea change matching (repo,index,kind) is wrongly suppressed; (2) DUPLICATE webhook — Gitea retries deliver the same webhook twice; the first consumes echo_pending=0, so the duplicate is NOT suppressed and leaks an echo to Nostr. Fix: replace the one-shot flag with a time-windowed, content-fingerprinted, NON-consuming guard: on reflection record echo_armed_at + echo_fingerprint (hash of the content the bridge wrote — issue title/body, comment body, state, PR head tip); ConsumeReflectedGiteaEcho suppresses any matching webhook within a short TTL window (default ~5m) AND matching fingerprint (so duplicates within the window are all suppressed and unrelated same-(repo,index,kind) user edits with different content are published); guards past the TTL are treated expired (disarmed lazily/periodically) so a dropped webhook never blocks genuine later events.
acceptance_criteria: duplicate delivery of a reflected webhook is suppressed every time within the window; a dropped webhook expires so a genuine later same-object change is published; a genuine user edit with different content within the window is NOT suppressed (fingerprint mismatch); expired guards are cleaned up; tests cover duplicate, dropped/expired, and fingerprint-mismatch cases
close_reason: Echo guard hardened: internal/echofp per-kind fingerprints; reflected_events.echo_armed_at+echo_fingerprint; CheckReflectedGiteaEcho is windowed (5m), fingerprint-matched, NON-consuming (duplicate-safe) with lazy DisarmExpiredEchoGuards (dropped-safe); webhook+reflector compute matching fingerprints. Tests cover duplicate/dropped/mismatch/expiry. Gate green.

title: Implement NIP-34 PR-update (kind:1619) reflection — update existing Gitea PR head branch
description: Follow-up to phase1-2gq. The reflector creates Gitea PRs from 1617/1618 but ignores 1619 (PR-update). A 1619 changes the tip of an existing PR (NIP-22 tags: E=pull-request-event-id of the root 1618, P=author, c=updated tip, clone). Implement: resolve the root PR via the E tag -> reflected_events row (gitea index + stored head branch), fetch the new c tip from clone URLs, update refs/heads/<head-branch> to the new tip in the bare repo, record the 1619 reflection (KindPRUpdate) to arm the echo guard, and make handlePR skip the resulting 'synchronized' webhook. Requires persisting the PR head branch at create time (add a column to reflected_events).
acceptance_criteria: a verified 1619 referencing a reflected root PR updates that PR's head branch ref to the new tip and records a reflected row; unknown/unreflected root E is ignored; head branch is recovered from storage (add reflected_events.gitea_head_branch, set on PR create); webhook synchronized echo is skipped; tests with temp bare repo. Gitea PR-head-sync caveat documented.
close_reason: 1619 PR-update reflection: reflected_events.gitea_head_branch persists the PR head at create; reflectPRUpdate resolves root via NIP-22 E tag -> reflected KindPROpen row, validates c tip, fetches it, force-updates refs/heads/<HeadBranch>, records KindPRUpdate (echo guard); handlePR skips reflected synchronized events. Gitea branch-sync caveat documented. Tests + gate green incl -tags full.

title: Implement full NIP-34 patch apply (kind:1617) — apply patch to a branch + open Gitea PR
description: Follow-up from Phase F (phase1-ki5). The reflector currently only records/fetches a 1617 patch tip to refs/nostr/<id> and logs that full apply is deferred. Implement real application: take the 1617 git-format-patch content (and threaded series via NIP-10 e-reply), apply it onto the base branch in a temp work area, push a branch into the bare repo, and open a Gitea pull request (base<-patch branch) via a new gitea client CreatePullRequest. Record reflected_events + echo-loop guard so the resulting Gitea PR webhook does not bounce back to Nostr. Sig-verify the event first.
acceptance_criteria: a verified 1617 for a provisioned repo applies onto base, creates a branch, and opens a Gitea PR; reflected_events row recorded; malformed/non-applying patch is handled gracefully (no crash, logged); unprovisioned/invalid-sig ignored; tests with fake Gitea + temp git repo
close_reason: Implemented: reflector opens a Gitea PR from Nostr 1617/1618 via two paths — (1) fetch c-tip into refs/nostr/<id> -> head branch (git update-ref) -> resolve base from bare-repo HEAD -> CreatePullRequest; (2) content format-patch -> temp detached worktree + git am -> head branch -> PR. Graceful fallback to recordPatchOnly + worktree cleanup on any failure; branch-name safety vs base; records KindPROpen for echo guard; handlePR skips reflected PR webhooks. 1619 update deferred. gitea CreatePullRequest added; 1618 subscribed. Tests + gate green incl -tags full.

title: Phase E: Full NIP-34 compliance — spec tag schemas for PR/patch/issue/status, euc, maintainers, NIP-22 comments
description: Plan section 6 / 9-E in docs/designs/user-signed-nip34-migration.md. CORRECTION: NIP-34 (nips/34.md in workspace) DOES define kinds 1618 (PR) and 1619 (PR update) as first-class kinds — they are KEPT, not retired. The real gap is the tag schema of events we already emit. Fix: (1) PR 1618 — use 'subject' (not 'title'), 'r'=earliest-unique-commit (not a human path), add 'c' (tip commit-id), 'clone', 'branch-name'; drop non-spec 'head'/'base'. (2) PR-update 1619 is tip-change ONLY — add required NIP-22 'E'/'P' referencing the PR, 'c', 'merge-base'; move close/reopen to status events, not 1619. (3) Issue 1621 — 'subject' not 'title'; drop non-spec 'r'/'action'. (4) Patches 1617 — 't root'/'root-revision', 'commit'/'parent-commit'/'commit-pgp-sig'/'committer'. (5) Status 1630-1633 — 'e' root/reply markers, multiple 'p', and 'q'/'merge-commit'/'applied-as-commits'. (6) Replies via NIP-22 kind 1111. (7) euc computed at provisioning; maintainers tag on announcements. Use go-nostr/nip34 helpers.

title: handlePatchPush is a stub — refs/nostr patch pushes never emit kind:1631 applied status
description: internal/webhook/handler.go handlePatchPush() (lines ~336-346) contains 'For now, just log — full implementation would fetch from relay' and returns nil without doing work. When a client pushes to refs/nostr/<event-id> (ngit patch workflow), the bridge should (a) fetch the pre-published kind:1617 patch event from the configured relays (or synthesize a minimal one from push metadata) and (b) emit a kind:1631 (applied) status event referencing that patch and the repo. close_reason: Implemented: handlePatchPush now (1) validates the refs/nostr/<id> is a 64-hex event id, (2) best-effort fetches the referenced kind:1617 patch via new publisher.FetchEvent (relay QuerySync), and (3) publishes a kind:1631 applied status with e=<patch-id>, a=30617:<hex>:<repo>, p=maintainer(+patch author when resolved), and applied-as-commits=<pushed SHA>. Emission is resilient to fetch failure/propagation lag since the git ref push is authoritative. Note: the bridge intentionally does NOT synthesize+sign a kind:1617 when absent — that would misattribute contributor authorship to the bridge key; the applied-status carries the landed commit instead.
